title: Christiano bockelmanno sedinensi, Pomerano, ... Johannes gundermannus hilperhusanus francus.
shelf_note: A 1598 Stettin gratulatory Latin poem (propempticon) for a student leaving home; no tradition or collection is assigned, so nothing it can be off-shelf from. It is humanist occasional verse, not esoterica.
structure_note: Page 5 is the title page (handwritten '37 a' folio, signature 'G' under the imprint), page 7 is signed 'A 2', so pages 1–4 are probably binding or preceding items in a Sammelband. 14 pages, all OCR'd, 8 translated; nothing broken in this run.

tr_errors.source: iuveni Eruditae humanitatis, et humanae eruditionis, patriâ Studiorum gratiâ abeunti
tr_errors.english: a young man / Going away to foreign lands for the sake of learned humanity and human learning
tr_errors.problem: The genitives describe the young man ('of learned humanity and humane learning'), and he is leaving his HOMELAND (patriâ) 'for the sake of studies'. The translation drops 'studiorum gratiâ' and invents 'to foreign lands'.

other.note: <vocab> lists 'Joachim Rhete, Andreas Kellner', who are not on the page (the imprint says only 'Typis Kellnerianis')

ocr_errors.ocr: Capta, movet laudis quae generosus amor?
ocr_errors.image: Cæpta, movet laudis quæ generosus amor?
ocr_errors.problem: cæpta (begun) misread as capta (captured); the translation follows it ('love of praise you have captured')

ocr_errors.image: printed italic type
ocr_errors.problem: The page is tagged as handwritten but it is printed

tr_errors.source: Quis verò credat, non, Bockelmanne, canendum Cæpta, movet laudis quæ generosus amor?
tr_errors.english: But who would believe, Bockelmann, that there is no song to be sung, which moves the generous love of praise you have captured?
tr_errors.problem: This should read 'Who would believe, Bockelmann, that what generous love of praise has begun is not worth singing?' The translation misconstrues the line from the 'capta' misreading.

tr_errors.source: Ast ego sus certè videor docuisse Minervam
tr_errors.english: But I surely seem to have taught Minerva
tr_errors.problem: 'sus' (the pig) is dropped. The proverb 'sus Minervam', a pig teaching Minerva, is the poet's self-mockery; without it the line reads as a boast.

book_verdict: Clean transcription of a short 1598 occasional poem. The translations are readable but loose: one misread ('Capta' for 'Cæpta'), a dropped proverb and a garbled title-page dedication. Nothing an expert would flag on sight.

title: Book of hours
shelf_note: A small illuminated Latin manuscript book of hours with a metal clasp (Harvard). No tradition is assigned; it fits a primary-source library as devotional liturgy.
structure_note: 330 pages, 321 translated. A pencil folio '80' is visible on page 163. The scans show one page with colour bars beside it, so each image is the reading page. Nothing odd.

tr_errors.problem: The opening word is the end of 'in tecto' (Ps 101:8, a sparrow 'on the housetop'), not 'covered'; this is a seam from the previous page

ocr_errors.image: the same rounded humanist bookhand as the other pages
ocr_errors.problem: wrong script description, and it is inconsistent with pages 82 and 163

title: [Collection containing 1 Mass, 2 Glorias, 1 Sanctus (fragmentary), 1 Te Deum, 3 hymns, 42 motets, ... 2 textless pieces
shelf_note: A 16th-century music manuscript (Regensburg Proske-Bibliothek C 120, the label is visible on page 16) is a real primary source. As held here it is mensural notation in microfilm strips, which is not a readable or translatable text, so the language 'Latin' and the translation lane do not fit it.
structure_note: Every 'page' is a thin contact-print strip (about 2000×220 px) with about six whole openings of the book, held by hands. Each record is therefore many leaves and nothing is legible at this size (I5/I7). The 30 pages, all 'translated', are 30 model descriptions of strips.

ocr_errors.image: six openings of mensural notation in one strip, illegible at this resolution
ocr_errors.problem: No transcription. The 'OCR' is a generic description of what a 16th-century partbook contains, including claims about clefs and underlay that cannot be seen at this size.

ocr_errors.ocr: <note>The provided image is a composite of multiple openings ... The following is a representation of the structural layout</note>
ocr_errors.problem: The model's commentary is stored as page text

tr_errors.english: ### Musical Content Overview ...
tr_errors.problem: The 'translation' is the English description again; nothing on the page is translated

other.note: A strip of six openings of notation is presented to readers as a prose page with an invented heading 'Musical Content Overview'

ocr_errors.ocr: The text labels identified within the musical staves include: Superius, Altus, Tenor, Bassus
ocr_errors.image: no voice labels are legible at 220 px height; only the archive card 'Regensburg Proske-Bibliothek C 120 ... II' can be made out
ocr_errors.problem: Voice-part labels are asserted that cannot be read in the image, which is likely confabulated from what partbooks usually carry

ocr_errors.image: six openings, some with blank staves
ocr_errors.problem: description instead of transcription

tr_errors.english: Tenor <gloss>Holding voice</gloss>
tr_errors.problem: Glosses are added to labels that are not legible on the page; the page itself is not translated

other.note: <summary>This page identifies the standard voice-part designations ...</summary> and <keywords> are stored in the reader translation

ocr_errors.ocr: Due to the high-level perspective of the scan, individual words are not legible ... Marginalia and annotations in a cursive humanistic hand.
ocr_errors.image: illegible strip of six openings
ocr_errors.problem: Description instead of transcription. It admits the text is illegible yet asserts 'Superius/Tenor/Bassus' headers and humanist marginalia.

tr_errors.english: The manuscript is likely a choirbook ...
tr_errors.problem: a model description translated as if it were the page

other.note: <summary>This page discusses the general contents of the manuscript ...</summary> and <keywords> leak into the reader text

book_verdict: Not a readable text. Each page is a microfilm contact strip of about six openings of music, and every 'transcription' and 'translation' is a model's generic description of a partbook, with labels it could not have read. It should be withdrawn from the OCR and translation lanes, and readers should not be shown it as 30 translated pages.

title: De morbius et officys vivendi
shelf_note: A 15th-century manuscript of Jacobus de Cessolis' chess allegory (the chapters on the pawns as the smith and the city guards, Frederick II's Capua gate). It is a legitimate primary source, but the catalogue title 'De morbius et officys vivendi' is garbled; the usual title is De moribus hominum et officiis nobilium (super ludo scaccorum).
structure_note: Pencil leaf numbers match the run: page 21 = 9, page 39 = 18, page 57 = 27, two images per leaf. But the OCR tags page 21 as <page-num>1</page-num> where the leaf reads 9. The title is misspelled (I7, moderate).

book_verdict: A genuine 15th-century Cessolis manuscript with a misspelled catalogue title. The bastarda reading is shaky. On two of three pages the OCR substitutes plausible but wrong sentences (an invented Ovid line, 'amicitia' for 'amentia', an invented maxim on rashness), and the fluent translation carries them to the reader.
